svg.title: Allocate a $45,000 Reference Startup Capital Plan
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-45000-reference-plan; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate a $45,000 Reference Startup Capital Plan; subtitle: Four buckets compare $15,000 lean, $45,000 reference, and $80,000 expanded plans.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: USD. Numeric values represent the $45,000 central/reference plan within the canonical $15,000–$80,000 startup range; value and detail text show the lean and expanded alternatives. All three plans assume a $75,000 BMC-84 bond, not a fully funded BMC-85 trust. Security allocations cover illustrative premium, provider charges, and any required collateral only if actual underwriting fits the allowance. Bond face value is not cash available to the brokerage. Verify current requirements and quotes before launch; restricted collateral cannot also fund carrier payments or operating runway.; caption: Lean: $3,000 + $4,000 + $6,000 + $2,000 = $15,000. Reference: $5,000 + $15,000 + $20,000 + $5,000 = $45,000. Expanded: $8,000 + $30,000 + $34,000 + $8,000 = $80,000. Bucket order is bond security, carrier working capital, operating runway, and setup. These launch budgets do not fully fund Base-volume payment gaps or guarantee runway through the 2–6 month first-deal window; phase spending, limit load exposure, or arrange additional funding.; stages: label: Broker bond premium and security allowance; value: Lean $3,000; reference $5,000; expanded $8,000; numeric value: 5000.0; detail: Allocate $3,000 of the $15,000 lean plan, $5,000 of the $45,000 reference plan, or $8,000 of the $80,000 expanded plan to quoted BMC-84 premium, provider charges, and any required collateral. These are planning allowances, not guaranteed quotes. If underwriting exceeds the allocation, revise funding before launch; do not substitute a partial BMC-85 trust or count restricted collateral as working cash.; label: Carrier payment working capital; value: Lean $4,000; reference $15,000; expanded $30,000; numeric value: 15000.0; detail: Reserve $4,000 of the $15,000 lean plan, $15,000 of the $45,000 reference plan, or $30,000 of the $80,000 expanded plan for carrier-payment timing gaps. Base carrier purchases of $2,550,000 annually require about $139,726 for a 20-day gap before buffers, so none of these allocations supports that exposure. Shorten collection terms, obtain deposits, reduce load volume, or secure additional committed funding.; label: Launch operating runway; value: Lean $6,000; reference $20,000; expanded $34,000; numeric value: 20000.0; detail: Reserve $6,000 of the $15,000 lean plan, $20,000 of the $45,000 reference plan, or $34,000 of the $80,000 expanded plan for pre-revenue operations and initial staffing. At $6,000 monthly burn, these fund about 1.0, 3.3, and 5.7 months respectively. The canonical monthly opex range is $6,000–$30,000, so higher burn shortens runway. None guarantees six months; phase hiring and spending or arrange additional funding without double-counting carrier working capital.; label: Setup systems and administration; value: Lean $2,000; reference $5,000; expanded $8,000; numeric value: 5000.0; detail: Allocate $2,000 of the $15,000 lean plan, $5,000 of the $45,000 reference plan, or $8,000 of the $80,000 expanded plan to registration work, process-agent services, contract preparation, TMS configuration, verification onboarding, and accounting setup. Obtain actual quotes and prioritize required launch controls. Keep one-time setup charges separate from bond costs and recurring operating-runway spending.

text.title: Allocate a $45,000 Reference Startup Capital Plan
text.tspan: Allocate a $45,000 Reference Startup Capital Plan

text.title: Broker bond premium and security allowance

rect.title: label: Broker bond premium and security allowance; numeric value: 5000.0; value: Lean $3,000; reference $5,000; expanded $8,000; detail: Allocate $3,000 of the $15,000 lean plan, $5,000 of the $45,000 reference plan, or $8,000 of the $80,000 expanded plan to quoted BMC-84 premium, provider charges, and any required collateral. These are planning allowances, not guaranteed quotes. If underwriting exceeds the allocation, revise funding before launch; do not substitute a partial BMC-85 trust or count restricted collateral as working cash.

text.title: Broker bond premium and security allowance: Lean $3,000; reference $5,000; expanded $8,000
text.tspan: Broker bond premium and security allowance: Lean $3,000; reference $5,000; expanded $8,000

rect.title: label: Carrier payment working capital; numeric value: 15000.0; value: Lean $4,000; reference $15,000; expanded $30,000; detail: Reserve $4,000 of the $15,000 lean plan, $15,000 of the $45,000 reference plan, or $30,000 of the $80,000 expanded plan for carrier-payment timing gaps. Base carrier purchases of $2,550,000 annually require about $139,726 for a 20-day gap before buffers, so none of these allocations supports that exposure. Shorten collection terms, obtain deposits, reduce load volume, or secure additional committed funding.

text.title: Carrier payment working capital: Lean $4,000; reference $15,000; expanded $30,000
text.tspan: Carrier payment working capital: Lean $4,000; reference $15,000; expanded $30,000

rect.title: label: Launch operating runway; numeric value: 20000.0; value: Lean $6,000; reference $20,000; expanded $34,000; detail: Reserve $6,000 of the $15,000 lean plan, $20,000 of the $45,000 reference plan, or $34,000 of the $80,000 expanded plan for pre-revenue operations and initial staffing. At $6,000 monthly burn, these fund about 1.0, 3.3, and 5.7 months respectively. The canonical monthly opex range is $6,000–$30,000, so higher burn shortens runway. None guarantees six months; phase hiring and spending or arrange additional funding without double-counting carrier working capital.

text.tspan: Launch operating runway: Lean $6,000; reference $20,000; expanded $34,000

rect.title: label: Setup systems and administration; numeric value: 5000.0; value: Lean $2,000; reference $5,000; expanded $8,000; detail: Allocate $2,000 of the $15,000 lean plan, $5,000 of the $45,000 reference plan, or $8,000 of the $80,000 expanded plan to registration work, process-agent services, contract preparation, TMS configuration, verification onboarding, and accounting setup. Obtain actual quotes and prioritize required launch controls. Keep one-time setup charges separate from bond costs and recurring operating-runway spending.
